newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INTERVIEW - Newsnet sees European growth.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Newsnet sees European growth.

text.p: Australian facsimile services group Newsnet ITN Ltd said it sees the best potential for short term growth from its European operations as it harvests the fruits of an agreement with the Czech-based APP Group.

"Our energies are being particularly directed at the moment towards Europe because the results of our strategic partnership with the APP Group should be reaped within the 12 month period," Newsnet's chief financial officer, Peter Blackie, told Reuters.

Newsnet, which listed on the Australian Stock Exchange in May 1995, operates an international fax node network which allows clients to complete international faxing cheaper than on a standard telephone network.
The company reported operating profit before abnormals of A$2.13 million in the year to June 30 against a loss of A$280,000 a year earlier.
Sales rose to A$24.4 million from A$15.6 million.
Towards the end of the 1995/96 financial year, Newsnet entered into an agreement with Australia's largest reseller, AAP Telecommunications (AAPT).
AAPT, which owns 8.5 percent of Newsnet, was given exclusive distribution rights to sell Newsnet's fax products in Australia.
"Following our agreement with AAPT, our entire strategy for Australia is now different," Blackie said.
"As far as penetrating the Australian market is concerned, we made a strategic decision to form an alliance with AAPT. Their customer base is far larger than the Newsnet customer base," he said.

"We expect the number of countries in which we operate in Europe to be at least 15 by next year and infrastructure and strategy is directed towards that growth in Europe at the moment," Blackie said in a telephone interview.
Newsnet is actively seeking resellers throughout Western and Eastern Europe, Blackie said. The company currently operates in 17 countries and 21 cities worldwide.
"By June 1997 we hope to increase the number of countries by about 15," Blackie said. He said Newsnet had a lot growth potential in all areas of the world including Australia.
Prior to the alliance with AAPT, Newsnet direct sold its products in Australia. "We would rather sell through a reseller, we believe we have picked a strong one in AAPT," he said.
Tighter market conditions in Australia last financial year, which curbed the company's growth, was a factor that influenced Newsnet to enter the agreement with AAPT, Blackie said.
Newsnet expected AAPT would be a major beneficiary of the deregulation of Australia's telecommunications industry.
"Our salesforce's job is to educate their (AAPT) salesforce about the benefits of the Newsnet system," Blackie said.
The largest player in the Australian fax services market is the government owned Telstra Corp, which has an estimated 65 to 70 percent share of business.

The remainder of the Australian market is largely controlled by Fax International, which is half-owned by Singapore Telecom, Pacific Star Services, wholly owned by Telecom Corp of New Zealand, AAPT's Medianet, Newsnet and Optus Telecommunications which offers fax services via its fixed line and mobile networks. A new entrant into the Australian market is the U.S.-based Xpedite Systems Inc.
"We understand Xpedite as a competitor. Whatever they are doing will be of interest to us," Blackie said.
"It's no different in other countries in which we compete against Xpedite but in most of those countries the reseller we deal with would be smaller than AAPT," he said.
Blackie said the Australian market was very competitive and he believed Pacific Star was looking to leave the market because of the losses it had experienced.
